blocks.useCase: These non-monotonic points are legitimate tier discounts, but an operator quoting by hand will hit them and conclude the system is wrong. Pinned so the shape is documented rather than disputed.

tests.title: makes a 7-day rental cheaper than a 6-day one, because the weekly rate lands
makes a 30-day rental cheaper than a 29-day one, because the monthly rate lands

blocks.describe: rental pricing — rounding
blocks.useCase: Rounding order decides whether the invoice total and the amount charged agree to the cent. Rounding per-day and rounding once at the end give different answers.

tests.title: returns exactly the weekly rate for 7 days even though 500/7 does not divide
rounds the accumulated fraction once at the end for 8 days
never returns a value with more than two decimal places

blocks.describe: rental pricing — a vehicle with no monthly rate configured
blocks.useCase: A live pricing defect: the tier fallback skips weekly for rentals of 30 days or more, so the renter is billed at the daily rate and one extra day costs 495.00 more.

tests.title: falls through to the DAILY rate at 30 days, making one extra day cost 495.00 more
should fall back to the weekly rate, not the daily rate, at 30 days

blocks.describe: rental pricing — a vehicle with no rates at all
blocks.useCase: An unpriced vehicle must yield 0 and an empty breakdown, never NaN. NaN propagates silently into the invoice and the Stripe amount.

tests.title: returns zero and an empty breakdown rather than NaN
still reports the day count when it cannot price the rental

blocks.describe: rental pricing — inputs the engine cannot price safely
blocks.useCase: Three inputs that produce a confident wrong number instead of an error — the worst failure mode for money code, because nothing downstream can tell it from a real price.

tests.title: returns a price of zero with a NaN day count when handed an ISO datetime
should price an ISO datetime the same as the date-only string it contains
silently bills a reversed date range as a single day instead of rejecting it
produces an infinite price when a tenant has monthly_tier_days set to zero
should never return a non-finite price, whatever monthly_tier_days holds
treats a negative monthly_tier_days the same hostile way

files.purpose: THE SIMPLE-RENTAL INVOICE — Layer 3 maths plus a Layer 1 contract on the composition. No network.

blocks.describe: invoice — the base rent, executed for real
blocks.useCase: The anchor figure the rest of the invoice is computed against. If this is wrong every proportional term (tax, service fee) is wrong with it.

tests.title: charges 89.00 x 3 = 267.00 for the three-day daily-tier rental

blocks.describe: invoice — extras
blocks.useCase: Extras are the one line the operator edits most, and per_day versus per_trip is a single string comparison away from billing three times too much or a third too little.

tests.title: bills a per-day extra once for every rental day: 15.00 x 1 x 3 = 45.00
bills a per-trip extra exactly once regardless of length: 25.00 x 1 = 25.00
treats a missing billing_type as per-trip, which is the historical default
bills 'PER_DAY' in the wrong case as a flat per-trip charge, because the check is exact
sums the selected extras to 70.00 and ignores the one not selected
skips a zero or negative quantity rather than billing it
skips a selected id that is not in the catalogue instead of throwing
multiplies by quantity: two seats for three days is 15.00 x 2 x 3 = 90.00
floors a fractional day count and never bills fewer than one day
returns extras unrounded, leaving rounding entirely to the caller

blocks.describe: invoice — Bonzah insurance, both taken and declined
blocks.useCase: The team lead asked for both paths by name. A declined coverage must contribute exactly 0 to the total, not absent and not NaN, because it is still a term in the sum.

tests.title: charges 26.95 x 3 = 80.85 for CDW alone on a three-day rental
charges nothing at all when the renter declines every coverage
prices all four coverages additively: 80.85 + 69.54 + 60.54 + 20.70 = 231.63
scales strictly linearly, with no multi-day discount

blocks.describe: invoice — the grand total, composed by hand from the real parts
blocks.useCase: Proves the eight terms compose to the figure a human gets on paper, and quantifies what widening the tax base would cost (55.32 on one three-day rental).

tests.title: sums to 953.895 for the scenario at the top of this file
would be 55.32 higher if tax were charged on the whole invoice instead of the rent
carries a sub-cent residue, because nothing in the chain rounds to cents

blocks.describe: invoice — the composition contract, read from the shipped source
blocks.useCase: The composition lives in a React component and cannot be imported, so its shape is asserted from source. Catches the change that actually happens: someone widens the tax base or adds a ninth term.

tests.title: computes tax on the discounted vehicle total, not on the whole invoice
computes a percentage service fee on the same narrow base as tax
builds the grand total from exactly the eight expected terms
does not round anywhere in the composition, which is why the residue survives
excludes the deposit from the total on the HOLD path and includes it on the CHARGED path
returns a zero deposit when the operator has turned deposits off entirely
drops the Bonzah premium to zero once the quote attempt has failed

files.purpose: RENTAL CREATION — the first step of the team lead's spine. Layer 1, offline.

blocks.describe: rental create — the vehicle double-booking guard
blocks.useCase: Two rentals on one vehicle for the same window means one renter arrives to find no car. The trigger is the only thing preventing it, so its blind spots are the risk.

tests.title: refuses a second rental for the same vehicle over an overlapping window
ignores rentals that are Cancelled, Rejected or Closed when looking for a clash
treats an open-ended rental as occupying the vehicle until the end of time
lets an extension push its own end date out without clashing with itself
cannot see a rental whose status is NULL, so such a rental blocks nothing
should guard the status comparison against NULL
takes no lock, so two simultaneous bookings of one vehicle can both commit

blocks.describe: rental create — the row both paths write
blocks.useCase: RLS is off on the core tables, so tenant isolation and correct dates are entirely the application's job at insert time. A row written wrong here is wrong forever.

tests.title: stamps tenant_id on the portal insert, because RLS is off on this table
sets an explicit status on both insert paths rather than leaving it NULL
stores an open-ended pay-as-you-go rental with a null end_date
formats the picker date with format(), never toISOString(), on the portal path
has no dropoff_time column anywhere — the columns are pickup_time and return_time

blocks.describe: rental create — rentals.monthly_amount means two different things
blocks.useCase: The same column holds an operator-entered monthly rate from the portal and a whole invoice total from the booking site. Anything that re-bills from it over-charges by the deposit and tax.

tests.title: stores the operator-entered monthly rate when the portal creates the rental
stores the entire invoice total when the booking site creates the rental
offers no discriminator on the row itself beyond which app wrote it

blocks.describe: rental create — availability rules that are not enforced at insert
blocks.useCase: Tier toggles and minimum durations are advisory in the widget and re-checked nowhere, so a booking the operator disabled is still written to the database.

tests.title: does not check the vehicle tier-availability toggles on the customer path
does not check the tenant minimum rental duration on the customer path
should re-check tier availability where the rental row is written

files.purpose: THE SPINE'S PAYMENT STEP — the four ways money is taken. Layer 1, offline.

blocks.describe: method 1 — auto charge on a stored card
blocks.useCase: An unattended charge that runs twice takes the renter's money twice, and a cron is exactly where a retry happens unseen. This is the only path in the whole payment surface that guards against it, so it is the reference standard.

tests.title: refuses to run without a caller-supplied request id
derives its Stripe idempotency key from the rental and that request id
persists the request id on the payment row so a duplicate can be recognised later

blocks.describe: method 2 — the on-screen checkout, and what it writes before payment
blocks.useCase: A row written before the customer pays must not claim the money arrived. Anything reading capture_status to decide "is this paid?" would treat an unpaid link as settled.

tests.title: records a not-yet-paid checkout as requiring capture and pending verification
explains in source why capture_status is requires_capture on the Stripe path
stamps payment_date at link creation, which is not when the money arrived

blocks.describe: method 3 — the same checkout link, emailed
blocks.useCase: The team lead was explicit that this is the SAME link, not a second payment mechanism. If it ever diverges, two operators doing what they believe is the same action produce different rows.

tests.title: accepts a payment URL created elsewhere rather than minting its own
can also create its own session, which is a second and differently-behaved path

blocks.describe: method 4 — a manually recorded payment
blocks.useCase: A hand-entered payment is the operator asserting money arrived outside Stripe. It must be distinguishable from a Stripe-settled one, or reconciliation against the Stripe dashboard can never balance.

tests.title: records the operator-supplied payment date rather than inventing one
is not marked auto-approved, because a human is the one asserting it

blocks.describe: the creators disagree about a payment that has not happened yet
blocks.useCase: Two creators write opposite values for the same situation. Whichever screen an operator happens to look at decides whether an unpaid rental looks paid — and one of them also skips the human verification queue entirely.

tests.title: marks an upfront checkout captured and auto-approved before the customer pays
should write the same not-yet-paid state as every other creator
should give every payment creator the idempotency guard auto-charge already has

files.purpose: THE SPINE'S EMAIL AND NOTIFICATION STEP — Layer 1, offline, source-of-record.

blocks.describe: the emailed-payment-link journey — does the operator get told?
blocks.useCase: The team lead's own worked example. If this chain breaks, an operator emails a payment link and is never told the customer paid — so the rental sits unactioned while the money is already banked.

tests.title: raises the operator's portal bell from a database trigger on payments, not from the webhook
emits nothing from the webhook itself, and says so in its own comment
flips the pre-created payments row from Pending to Completed when Stripe settles
sends the operator's email through a second trigger on notifications, via pg_net

blocks.describe: the operator-email dispatch is pinned to one project
blocks.useCase: A staging or branch database silently lacks the operator email entirely, so any Layer 2 run there would "prove" a path that only works in production. This is the assertion that stops that false confidence.

tests.title: posts to a hardcoded production URL rather than a per-database setting
should resolve its own project URL instead of naming one environment

blocks.describe: the two emailed-payment-link paths disagree about the customer's receipt
blocks.useCase: The renter pays and never receives a receipt, so support fields "did my payment go through?" for every operator-emailed link. Two paths that look identical to the operator behave differently.

tests.title: attaches a receipt address when send-invoice-email creates the session itself
attaches no receipt address when the portal creates the session first
also suppresses the webhook's own customer notification for portal-initiated payments
should confirm the payment to the customer however the link was created

blocks.describe: the test and live webhooks stay in step on notification behaviour
blocks.useCase: Both webhooks must behave identically. A notification that fires in test mode but not live — or the reverse — is the hardest class of bug to see, because every rehearsal passes.

tests.title: gates the customer notification the same way in both modes
leaves the operator bell to the database in both modes

blocks.describe: a failed notification never rolls back a settled payment
blocks.useCase: A failed email must never undo a successful payment. If a sender throws inside the settlement path, Stripe has the money and our ledger does not.

tests.title: dispatches the operator email fire-and-forget, so a dead function cannot block the insert
reports success from aws-ses-email even when no message was sent

files.purpose: THE SPINE'S AGREEMENT STEP, and the sync back from the processor. Layer 1, offline.

blocks.describe: the agreement records which mode it was created under
blocks.useCase: A document created in test mode but fetched with the live API key returns nothing, so the signed agreement silently never arrives. The mode must travel with the record, not be re-derived from whatever the tenant is set to now.

tests.title: reads the tenant's BoldSign mode and brand when the document is created
resolves the mode from the agreement first, then the rental, then the tenant
defaults to test rather than live when nothing records a mode
selects boldsign_mode on every rental and agreement read in the webhook

blocks.describe: the automation send path reports email delivery it never measured
blocks.useCase: The operator sees a green "sent" for an email nobody received, so nobody chases the signature and the rental stalls with an unsigned agreement.

tests.title: tells BoldSign not to email the signer, because we send that mail ourselves
returns a hardcoded emailSent:true without invoking send-signing-email
should measure the signing email like the other two send paths do

blocks.describe: the sync back — what the rental may believe before the processor confirms
blocks.useCase: The rental's payment state must come from the processor confirming settlement, never from us having asked for it. Anything that writes "paid" before the webhook lands turns an abandoned checkout into a free rental.

tests.title: promotes the payment to Completed only when the settlement event arrives
treats the expiry event as a distinct outcome from a completed one
never lets a Square submission response stand in for settlement
